reconcile.note: Gill resolves both the headcount and direction problems by positing three separate blind men healed in two encounters at Jericho, one on approach and two on departure.

discrepancy.note: Strauss presses both the headcount and the entering-versus-leaving-Jericho divergence as a genuine contradiction among the Synoptics.

quotes.text: Matthew having two blind men, the two other Evangelists only one; and also as to its locality, Luke making it take place on the entrance of Jesus into Jericho, Matthew and Mark on his departure out of Jericho.
quotes.attr: David Friedrich Strauss (d. 1874), The Life of Jesus Critically Examined (1846), pt. II, ch. IX, on Matthew 20:30 and Luke 18:35.

sides.snippet: two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out
sides.verseText: Behold, two blind men sitting by the road, when they heard that Jesus was passing by, cried out, \"Lord, have mercy on us, you son of David!\"

sides.snippet: as he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
sides.verseText: It happened, as he came near Jericho, a certain blind man sat by the road, begging.
